title: Where the Pattern Breaks
statement: A weaving manual gives way to gears, then to anemones, fungi, insects, fish, and a drawn body. The collage follows the instruction only long enough to expose its structure; beyond that point, images begin to migrate, improvise, and make their own connective logic.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent where following an instruction ends and interpreting it begins.

actions.title: Where the Pattern Breaks
actions.statement: A weaving manual gives way to gears, then to anemones, fungi, insects, fish, and a drawn body. The collage follows the instruction only long enough to expose its structure; beyond that point, images begin to migrate, improvise, and make their own connective logic.

notes.note: Establishing a split composition: archival instruction and engineered mechanisms on one side, organic interpretation and embodied form on the other, joined by a horizontal bridge.

The canvas now reads as a staged passage from typographic rule to mechanical procedure to an interpretive figure, with the bridge acting as a threshold. I’m adding one organic fragment and one illustrated specimen cluster to make the transition visibly porous rather than purely diagrammatic.

The visual hierarchy is clear, but the organic threshold is still absent from the visible canvas. I’m surfacing it as the hinge between the mechanical panel and the drawn figure, and adding a narrow Morris textile strip as a repeated rule that can be read either as instruction or ornament.

The inspected canvas has a readable left-to-right descent from printed rule, through mechanism and organic threshold, into the figure and specimen imagery. I’m adding one directional fish form across the lower transition so the composition gains a visual gesture from prescribed diagram toward interpretation.

The inspected canvas now clearly stages instruction as a literal title page, procedure as gears and textile, and interpretation as the crossing of organic forms, figure, fish, insects, and bridge. The composition is visually resolved, so I’m recording the title and statement before a final unchanged review.
